name: RainyDayClicks
source:
It was raining again. Not that there was anything wrong with that, it was just an unfortunate day to take some pictures. But then again Sam never knew what to capture once he could actually walk through the gardens, parks and streets. 
 
 *click* 
 
 With the rain keeping him inside the house he had no choice but to watch TV or play a game on his PC. Sure he could take pictures of the rain but with only one camera he would n't risk it getting wet. So off to the living room he went. His father was there drinking his fifth cup of coffee while his mother slowly browsed through the channels. 
 
 *click* 
 
 Even with the ability to record several hundred hours of TV and a connection to the internet, it always felt like there was nothing to watch. Sam had learned not to disturb the parental routine of watching and flipping mindlessly, somehow it made things feel like home. 
 
 *click* 
 
 Getting to the PC would be easy, he just hoped that he could play at least one level before his Brother had to use the thing for something. It was always like that. No one needs the PC until Sam wants to play a game and with the rain settling in the chances are that he wo n't be left alone for long. 
 
 *click* 
 Do it slower... 
 *click* 
 *click* 
 FFS! 
 
 Nothing could take the joy of shooting another Russian in the face. Always taking up too much space on the servers. Sam was having fun playing BF4 and his friends had just logged in when he felt a tap on his shoulder. His brother was there, ready to chase him away and tell him he needed the PC for `` work''. Because looking at weird pictures and browsing the internet meant work. 
 
 *Click* 
 
 With the TV taken and PC being underused there was only one thing left that Sam could do. Lying in bed and reading a book. Sam had been reading mysteries lately and they had actually caused him to be a bit more paranoid in his everyday life. Just a few days before at College what Sam thought was a grand mystery, why the blonde girl that sits next to him had disappeared, was actually just a simple case of her getting tired of his weird hand movements. 
 
 *Click* 
 *Click* 
 stop it! 
 *Click* 
 *Click* 
 
 It was March again and Sam had Broken up with Alice, she was sweet but also amazingly negative... 
 
 *Click* 
 Dammit now we skipped several months, you know I ca n't read that fast. Stop skipping pages just because you find you're getting bored. We're all stuck in here with only the one Kindle. If you do n't stop I will slap some sense into you, you know once I can find the particles that my arms used to be. 
 
 Ziandar was n't enjoying being stuck in a black hole with his henchman. Somehow they had control of the Kindle and he was the only one that could see the screen. They just liked pressing the buttons. It looked like eternity was going to be a very, very long time...
retelling:
Narrated by Ziandar's Henchman:

In the depths of a churning abyss, I found myself ensnared in an unfathomable black hole, alongside my master, Ziandar. The void was a silent and menacing presence, swallowing all light and sound, save for the occasional echo of our own breaths. We were no longer mere prisoners; we had become spectral entities manipulating the fabric of reality itself.

One day, our reach extended beyond the confines of this cosmic prison, seeping into a distant world - Earth. Our target: a Kindle, owned by an insignificant creature named Sam. Unbeknownst to us, this device would become the conduit through which we could torment and amuse ourselves for eons to come.

As Sam sat in his cozy bedroom, engrossed in his mystery novel, our control over his Kindle began to take effect. The pages turned with a satisfying click, interrupting Sam's escape into the story. His frustration was palpable as he struggled to regain control of his device and immerse himself once more in the world of fiction.

Meanwhile, on the other side of the universe, Ziandar reveled in our newfound power. I could feel his excitement pulsating through the dark matter that bound us together. He commanded me to increase the frequency of our interruptions and to delve further into Sam's life, feeding off his emotions and using them to fuel our own existence.

As days turned into weeks, we grew bolder and more daring. We learned about Sam's past - the heartbreak he experienced with a girl named Alice and the challenges he faced at college. We laughed as he grew increasingly frantic in his attempts to shake off our influence and reclaim control of his life.

In the end, we were content to remain trapped in the black hole, feeding on Sam's life for all eternity. The dance between us was a never-ending symphony, a cosmic ballet of power and torment. And as I drifted off into the void, I knew that our story would continue for all time, an eternal reminder of the power of manipulation and control.
